findings.text: The `angular` option is only applied when the class has no `__rich_repr__`. For a class that defines its own `__rich_repr__` and uses `@auto(angular=True)`, the flag is silently dropped. `auto_repr` reads `angular` from `self.__rich_repr__`, so it falls back to False and the repr comes out as `Foo(...)` instead of `<Foo ...>`.

0.reason: The change only sets `cls.__rich_repr__.angular = angular` inside the `if not hasattr(cls, "__rich_repr__")` branch. So with `@auto(angular=True)` on a class that defines its own `__rich_repr__`, the flag is dropped: `auto_repr` reads `getattr(..., "angular", False)` and outputs `Foo(...)` instead of `<Foo ...>`. This is a separate defect from the reference bug's `==` vs `is` comparison.
